newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen firm, but some doubters.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen firm, but some doubters.

text.p: Belgian shares rose in early trade on Wednesday but dealers said the focus was on individual stocks rather than the broader market.
With many big investors still out for the Easter break, this trend would likely continue in the days ahead.
"The market seems to be calm again after the turbulence of last week, thanks to the higher dollar and bonds," one trader said. "It's even well oriented, but we don't see big orders."
At around 0915 GMT, the Bel-20 leading share index .BFX was up 9.88 points, or 0.47 percent, at 2,124.31 points, little changed since the start of trade.

Traders reported interest in photo processing group Spector, at present on a roadshow of the Brussels brokerages to present 1996 results. The results, released last week, were well received by investors despite a loss. Current earnings rose and the outlook remains firm for the company, dealers said.
Spector was up 80 francs, or 3.64 percent, at 2,280 francs, making it the market's biggest mover.
Oil group PetroFina attracted renewed interest, up 75 francs to 12,000 francs, on news of expansion of its U.S. petrochemicals activities.
Not all analysts agreed the market would hold.

"Take profits on stock positions and favour cash," Carl Coppieters at brokerage Cels Guigon Securities said in a note. "The markets are staying nervous and every bad U.S. indicator is punished with selling."

He was sceptical about expectations of profit growth this year, pointing to likely increases in interest rates, which would raise corporate financing charges, increase savings and cut into consumption.
Companies were also suffering from high wage costs.

He singled out Bekaert, unchanged at 21,600 francs, as a stock to be treated with caution since the company was suffering from overcapacity and the impact from a restructuring was not likely until 1999. francs in 1996 and forecast another loss this year, he noted.
Cockerill was up one franc at 136, building on gains made since an earnings news conference at which its chairman hinted he was open to an alliance for the group.
